name: traversal-identity-read-address
description: A structurally well-formed `read` address whose `element` is a path traversal. The envelope is right in every other respect — `{layer, element}`, no string path anywhere — so the refusal cannot come from the address *shape*; it comes from `$defs/identity`, which holds an element identity to a single path segment because the registry composes a file name from it.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model. `swc` is a declared layer and the request reaches it correctly; only the identity is hostile. Reads disclose no storage path, but the identity would still have to be resolved against the file system by the registry, which is where a traversal would land if it were admitted.

expected.notes: `schema-violation` and not `broken-reference`: the value never becomes an identity the engine could fail to resolve, because `protocol.schema.json` refuses the envelope first (pass A). That is the difference from `unknown-field-swc-safety-level.json`, whose address is legal and whose *meaning* only the registry can reject. `$defs/identity` refuses `.`, `..` and any value carrying `/`, `\` or NUL, so the rule is stated once and applies to every `element` in every request — the no-traversal rule made structural rather than delegated to a sanitizer.
